diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any interval $J \subset \RR$, we consider the Bochner space $\Ltwosp{J, \HHilb}$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inner product on L2(J,H) is defined by an integral from 0 to T, not over J. For arbitrary J this is not the Bochner inner product on L2(J,H) and does not define its norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the limits of integration in the Bochner inner product definition to J.
issues.overall_effect: The general J-dependent functional framework and the appendix weak-solution propositions are based on an incorrect L2(J) inner product definition.
issues.title: Bochner inner product integrates over the wrong interval
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the definition restores the stated Bochner-space framework without changing the main finite-interval results.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed map has domain and codomain L2(I,H), but the sentence claims it is an isomorphism from XX_H to H1(I,H). As written, the map is not the stated isomorphism.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed map by u in XX_H mapped to e^{itH}u in H1(I,H).
issues.overall_effect: The formal statement of Proposition prop: XX properties is internally inconsistent, and later proofs that cite this proposition's isomorphism part rely on the unstated corrected map.
issues.title: Misstated domain and codomain of the XX_H to H^1 isomorphism
issues.why_classification: The intended isomorphism is clear and the correction is local; it does not change the claimed Hilbert-space result.

dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.failure_explanation: In the second density argument, u_n is the spectral projection of u, not a mollification. Therefore (i∂t-H)u_n is not ρ_n * (1_I f) as written; the correct object would be the spectral projection of f.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect mollification identity by the spectral projection identity (i∂t-H)π_{(-n,n)}(H)u = π_{(-n,n)}(H)f and verify convergence in XX_H.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the density and integration-by-parts proposition is invalid as written; results that cite its integration-by-parts formula inherit this gap until repaired.
issues.title: Density proof falsely identifies spectral projection with time mollification
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is standard and the repair is a local correction of the density argument, with no loss of the stated result.

dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.failure_explanation: The displayed bound mixes the integration variable s with a free t inside an L2(I,H) norm, and uses ∂_t v(s) where the Duhamel representation requires a well-defined function of t. As written, this is not a valid estimate of ||Au||_{L2(I,H)}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the estimate using u(t)=e^{-itH0}v(t), v(t)=v(0)+∫_0^t ∂_s v(s)ds, the Kato-smoothing estimate for A e^{-isH0}, and Cauchy-Schwarz to obtain the claimed bound independent of T up to the stated factor.
issues.overall_effect: The central norm-equivalence theorem is not proved as written, and all results that invoke it, including the space-time variational formulation, improved estimate, many-body corollary, and dual formulation, are unsupported until the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Invalid estimate in proof of Theorem th: XX0 XX equality
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and does not change the theorem, but it requires a nontrivial correction of the central estimate rather than a one-line typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The functional F in the corollary contains the bounded time-dependent term B(t), but the proof computes an expression with only A. Consequently F(v) is not equal to ||u-u*||^2_{XX_H} when B is nonzero, and the proof does not establish the claimed estimate in the B≠0 case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include B(t) in the computation and use the time-dependent norm equivalence from Theorem th: XX0 XX equality to bound the B-term.
issues.overall_effect: The stated variational formulation and error-equivalence constants are proved only in the B=0 case as written; the advertised time-dependent B case is unsupported.
issues.title: Corollary proof omits the B(t) term
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the stated conclusion remains available once the B(t) term is handled.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that under H0-smoothness the estimate can be replaced by ||Au||_{L2(I,H)} ≤ C ||u||_{XX_H0}, but this T-independent bound is not established. The cited adaptation of the base estimate does not yield the improved √(1+T) rate without that missing argument.

failure_location.quote: notice that if $A$ is $H_0$-smooth, then \eqref{equtmp:0} in the proof above can be replaced by

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the T-independent L2 estimate for Au from H0-smoothness and the H1(I,H) characterization of XX_H0, or weaken the theorem to the rate already proved without that estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The improved norm equivalence is unsupported as written, and Theorem th:Schro, which is stated as a direct corollary of it, inherits this gap.
issues.title: Improved theorem proof omits the needed smoothing estimate
issues.why_classification: A contained smoothing argument is needed; if not supplied, the advertised improved rate is lost.

dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition states a nontrivial equality of final-time-zero spaces and norm equivalences, but the only justification is a phrase saying it is proved analogously. No proof is given, and the endpoint T changes the estimates and well-posedness argument in a non-routine way.

failure_location.quote: We then have the following result, which is proved analogously to Theorem \ref{th: XX0 XX equality}, simply by taking the integrals from $T$ to $t$ instead of $0$ to $t$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a final-value version of the norm-equivalence proof, including the backward evolution formulation and the endpoint T estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The dual formulation, the S* estimates, and the L2 variational corollary depend on this unproved proposition.
issues.title: Dual space proposition is asserted without a proof
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is local to the dual formulation but nontrivial; without it, the subsequent dual results are unsupported.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the lower estimate chooses u solving (i∂t-H-B(t))u=w with u(T)=0, but this final-value solvability is not established. Without it, one cannot guarantee that w is in the range of the associated operator and the inf-sup/coercivity bound may fail.

failure_location.quote: define $u$ as the unique element of $\YY_{H_0}$ such that $(i\partial_t - H - B(t)) u = w$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove that for every w in L2(I,H) there is a unique u in YY_H0 solving (i∂t-H-B(t))u=w, e.g. by the backward Duhamel formula and the equality YY_H=YY_H0.
issues.overall_effect: The S* coercivity estimate is unsupported, and the L2 variational corollary, which uses this estimate, inherits the defect.
issues.title: S* lower bound assumes an unproved surjectivity property
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a standard but nontrivial final-value well-posedness argument; the statement is not established as written.

issues.failure_explanation: In the converse direction the proof replaces the pairing involving S* by one with (i∂t-H)e^{-itH}w, omitting the -B(t) term that is part of S*. Thus it proves at best the B=0 statement. In addition, the displayed equivalence (Id+(S0*)^{-1}(A+B(t)))u = ... is not well-typed as stated because (A+B(t))u is not an element of the antidual space on which (S0*)^{-1} acts.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Repair the converse by retaining B(t) and using the bounded perturbation B(t)u in the weak formulation; replace or correctly define the ill-typed operator equation.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed characterization of weak solutions by S* u = iδ0⊗u0+f is not proved for the time-dependent B case, and the corollary relying on this proposition is affected.
issues.primary_affected_tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.title: Proposition S-star connection drops B(t) and contains an ill-typed equivalence
issues.why_classification: The proof needs a substantive correction of the B-dependent argument, though the intended statement appears repairable.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is stated for the equation with B(t), and S* in the proof includes B(t), but the functional E* only contains A u. For B≠0 the displayed expression does not vanish at the solution u*, so the claimed minimizer and norm equivalence are false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term i∫_0^t e^{-i(t-s)H0}B(s)u(s)ds to the functional and correct the identification with (S0*)^{-1}S* accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The alternative L2 variational formulation is invalid for nonzero time-dependent bounded potentials B(t).
issues.title: L2 variational functional omits B(t)
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local correction of the functional; the intended result with the B-term included is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivative computation contains negative powers (-Δ+V(t))^{j-k} for j<k, which is not a valid expression for ∂t((-Δ+V(t))^k). Moreover, the theorem invokes u*∈XX_{-Δ} with J=R, although XX_H has only been defined for the finite interval I=(0,T).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the commutator formula for ∂t A(t)^k, justify the form-domain equivalence used to pass to H^k, and either define the global-in-time XX-space or restate the result in H1(R,H).
issues.overall_effect: The stated time-regularity estimate is not proved as written; the induction and the use of the XX-space on the whole line are defective.
issues.title: Regularity theorem proof contains an invalid commutator estimate and uses XX on R
issues.why_classification: The repair requires fixing the energy estimate and the global-line formulation, but does not affect the main finite-time variational results.

issues.failure_explanation: The text says C^L transforms a first-kind Chebyshev series into a second-kind series. The displayed matrix does not do this: for example, the relation T1=U1/2 implies U1=2T1, but the displayed matrix gives the corresponding coefficient 1/2 instead of 2. Thus the discrete quadratic form and linear system built with C^L do not represent the stated minimization problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace C^L by the correct linear map from T-basis coefficients to U-basis coefficients, or adjust the formula for the discrete quadratic form to use the inverse map consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed Chebyshev Galerkin discretization for the ODE and the analogous periodic scheme is not the discretization of the claimed variational problem as written.
issues.title: Chebyshev conversion matrix C is not the stated T-to-U conversion
issues.why_classification: The algorithmic object is wrong but the correction is local and does not change the continuous variational result.

issues.failure_explanation: The appendix defines (i∂t-H-B(t))u=f weakly by pairing u with (i∂t-H)φ. For B≠0 this is not the correct weak formulation; the test operator must include B(t)φ. With B a nonzero bounded self-adjoint operator, a strong solution of the B-equation need not satisfy the displayed identity.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add B(t)φ to the test operator in the appendix weak definition.
issues.overall_effect: The weak notion introduced in the appendix is false for the time-dependent B(t) equations the paper treats.
issues.title: Appendix weak definition omits B(t) in the test operator
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single term and restores the intended weak formulation.
